transcript:
[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jared from Redwood Inference — i handle the AtlasDocs account. today we want to walk through our hosted API for embeddings and the rerank endpoint, show a quick live demo, and leave time for your questions.
[00:12] Maya: Hi Jared, thanks — Maya here. Luis and Anita on from our side. we're trying to improve search relevance across our docs product, reduce noise for long-tail queries and speed up result quality without a big infra lift.
[00:25] Jared: perfect. Priya, do you want to kick off the demo?
[00:28] Priya: yeah thanks. i'll share my screen. quick agenda: 1) high-level arch, 2) embeddings endpoint usage and embedding dim tradeoffs, 3) candidate gen + rerank flow, 4) live demo of a rerank call and perf numbers, 5) q&a.
[00:45] Priya: at a high level teams do a two-stage pipeline: candidate generation (BM25 or ANN) then call our rerank endpoint that takes original query + candidate doc texts and returns a reordered list with scores. we also expose raw embeddings so you can do nearest neighbor if you prefer.
[01:03] Luis: is your rerank model hosted with the same runtime as the embeddings? i.e., latency implications?
[01:08] Priya: good q. we run both on our hosted fleet; embeddings are typically cheaper SIMDed ops, rerank calls are cross-encoder style and a bit heavier. typical p50 for embeddings is 15–35 ms for 1536-d on hosted, rerank p50 depends on candidate count — 5 docs ~80–120 ms, 10 docs ~150–250 ms. rough numbers, we have per-route dashboards.
[01:29] Anita: can you repeat the dims you support, and which you recommend for docs search?
[01:35] Priya: sure — common dims: 512, 768, 1536, 2048 depending on model. for AtlasDocs we usually recommend 1536 as a balance — good recall for short and mid-length docs, reasonable cost. if you're very cost-sensitive, 768 can still be decent with tuned rerank.
[01:50] Luis: our current pipeline is BM25 -> dense with Pinecone for ANN -> a small transformer reranker. cost is creeping up. how would Redwood fit?
[01:58] Jared: you can keep your BM25 for candidate gen, swap Pinecone for our hosted embeddings + ANN, or keep Pinecone and call our rerank. main advantage: single vendor for embeddings + rerank reduces egress/cost and we provide batching and prefix/KV caching to accelerate repeated queries.
[02:15] Luis: how many qps can you support on hosted? and if we need higher, is there a dedicated option?
[02:20] Priya: hosted supports bursty traffic fine — typical customers in the 50–500 qps range. for sustained throughput we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) — you get predictable latency SLOs and capacity guarantees.
[02:31] Tom: security is key — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), KMS integration, and ideally a VPC flow for sensitive data. can hosted meet that?
[02:40] Jared: hosted comes with SOC2 and we can plug into your SSO. for KMS and BYOK we have integrations; for full VPC/on-prem you can opt for Redwood Private — that is the on-prem/VPC deployment. For hosted we do encryption at rest and in transit and we have audit logs.
[02:56] Maya: are logs retained? we need 90-day audit logs for compliance.
[03:00] Jared: yes, audit logs are an add-on with configurable retention; default is 30 days but we can extend to 90+.
[03:06] Priya: ok demo screen — first i'll show the embeddings endpoint. simple REST POST /v1/embeddings with model param. here's a sample payload with text and we're getting back an array of floats (trimmed in demo). the notebook in the shared drive shows how to persist vectors into an index.
[03:28] [03:30] (screen scrolls, typing)
[03:35] Priya: i'm calling the embeddings endpoint with a batch of 16 docs. you can see latency per batch is 220 ms and throughput improves significantly vs single calls due to batching. watch the KV cache note — if you have repeated prefixes we avoid recompute.
[03:50] Luis: you said KV cash earlier? i think you meant KV cache :)
[03:52] Priya: yes, ha — KV cache, my typo.
[03:55] Priya: next i run a candidate gen — i have BM25 results locally and i'll send top-10 into the rerank endpoint. request format is query + candidates array (texts or ids with content). we also accept metadata and can return per-candidate features. the response includes a score and new order.
[04:15] Priya: running now... response in 170 ms for 10 candidates in this demo region (us-west). note p95 will be higher during peak; dashboards show breakdown p50/p95/p99.
[04:28] Maya: what scoring function is used? cosine on embeddings plus cross-encoder?
[04:33] Priya: common pattern: ANN or sparse to get candidates, then a cross-encoder reranker that produces final scores. you can also do hybrid scoring: embed similarity + reranker delta, or a lightweight linear comb of BM25 and embedding sim. we expose raw embedding sims if you want to compute yourself.
[04:51] Luis: do you support rerank on document chunks? our docs are long — we chunk and want a document-level score aggregation.
[04:58] Priya: yes — chunk then aggregate by max or weighted avg. we recommend a heuristics-based aggregator, or you can send candidates at chunk level and post-agg on client side. our SDK examples show chunk aggregation patterns.
[05:12] Anita: what's the pricing model for hosted? token-based or per-embedding?
[05:16] Jared: embeddings are priced per vector (unit) and rerank is priced per request+candidate count; we also include bundle discounts in pilot terms. i'll send the detailed pricing deck after.
[05:26] Tom: how about SSO — you mentioned SAML earlier, do you have SCIM for user provisioning?
[05:31] Jared: yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for org users. sometimes pronounced "Sam-el" or misheard in notes but it's standard SAML / SSO flows.
[05:40] Priya: quick note on reproducibility: you can pin model versions, we keep model catalog with performance profiles. if a rollout triggers regressions we have eval hooks and rollback policies in the console.
[05:52] Luis: do you let us host the model weights in our VPC if needed?
[05:56] Jared: that's supported under Redwood Private — you get a private control plane and customer-managed networking so model artifacts never leave your environment.
[06:04] Priya: demo: i swapped to a high-recall config — 20 candidates then rerank — see conversational query where recall improves but rerank latency increases. tradeoff conversation: if you want <100ms p50 rerank we suggest 5–6 candidates with a stronger embedding dim; for quality-focused use 15–30 candidates with a heavier reranker and offline batch rerank for nightly re-ranking.
[06:28] Maya: i like the caching note — many of our queries repeat. can you show how caching behaves?
[06:32] Priya: sure — here's a call where 60% of requests hit prefix cache — you can see latency drop 30–40%. caching works best when the repeated user queries share prefixes or you use session-level KV for chat flows.
[06:47] Luis: any recommended eval metrics? we track MRR and NDCG@10.
[06:52] Priya: those are good; we also surface precision@k, recall@k and A/B with human eval for tricky queries. we can hook eval regressions to alerting and tie to prompt sets.
[07:04] Anita: are there any limits on candidate text length?
[07:08] Priya: we have per-call token limits; long docs should be chunked. specifics depend on model; doc in the drive lists token limits per model.
[07:16] (short silence)
[07:20] Maya: ok next steps — we'd like a pilot: we can share a sample of queries and click labels, and we want a 2-week bench to compare current pipeline vs Redwood hosted rerank.
[07:30] Jared: sounds great. i'll send the pilot terms and pricing. Priya will drop the demo notebook and benchmark template.
[07:36] Luis: for the pilot do you need full dataset or a subset?
[07:39] Priya: start with top 10k queries + labeled clicks; that'll surface many issues. if you can provide example doc IDs and your BM25 outputs even better so we can replicate candidate gen.
[07:49] Tom: who will own the PoC in Redwood?
[07:52] Jared: i'll be the commercial owner; Priya will be lead SE on technical scope.
[07:57] Maya: perfect. thanks everyone.
[07:59] Jared: thanks all — we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites. bye.
[08:04] (call ends)
notes: Demo included live latencies: embeddings p50 15–35ms (1536-d), rerank 10-candidate ~170ms in us-west demo region
Caching (KV cache) reduced repeated query latency by ~30–40% in demo scenario
Pilot requested: top 10k queries + click labels, Redwood to provide notebook and trial API key
